decisions.reason: As a newly launched core safety-shoe line in the firm’s main business, it likely benefits from meaningful development and production investment, so management would tend to continue it rather than quickly admit a mistake.
The comfort insole is a less publicly emphasized accessory and therefore easier to withdraw than a flagship shoe line, but after a recent launch the firm would still be inclined to give it more time.

This supportive insole sits in a complementary niche with more limited visible commitment, yet the firm’s innovation orientation and recent investment make continued support more likely than early removal.
An ergonomic safety-shoe series presented on its own page signals strong public commitment in a strategically central category, which makes escalation of commitment especially likely.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a more specialized offering, but they still fit the firm’s protective-footwear identity and are recent enough for management to attribute any weak uptake to temporary market factors.
Being shown on the home page indicates visible commitment, and despite being an accessory product the firm is likely to persist because dropping it quickly would undercut a public launch signal.
